nodes.jar.text.t: "Deserters? There's a ravine to the northeast, four days from here. Everyone knows they're there, and nobody wants to go after them, because then they'd have to do something definite about them." The Captain rubs his forehead. "If you ever need somewhere to hide, you know where to look."

nodes.jar_list.options.[lapowka].text.t: The command has expensive seals. I've got sixty groats.

nodes.jar_list.options.[wymowa].text.t: That you've got thirty-two more men on the ramparts.

nodes.jar_list.text.t: The Captain stops writing. "A safe-conduct. For deserters. Thirty-two men who threw down their weapons when that same pike charge was going for their mates." He taps the pen on the notebook. "I've got three hundred who stayed. What do I tell them? That whoever runs comes back with a paper?"

nodes.jar_list_lapowka.text.t: The Captain looks at the coins, then at you. He doesn't pick them up, just sweeps them into a drawer with the notebook. "For dressings. We'll buy our own dressings." He writes, seals, and doesn't look your way again. "We never met over this. Though I'm not at all sure whether I'm talking about you just now, or about myself."

nodes.jar_list_nie.text.t: "You speak well. So did the man who led them onto the pikes." The Captain goes back to his notebook and rubs his forehead. "I won't write it. You've got other business, so see to it. If they want to come back without a paper, I won't run out of rope for them, and you won't have to feel bad that you didn't try."

nodes.jar_list_tak.text.t: The Captain is silent for a long time, then looks for a clean sheet he doesn't have and writes on the back of an order about hardtack. "No patches. No pay for three months. First on the ramparts." He seals it as if squashing a cockroach. "And don't tell anyone I let myself be talked into it."

nodes.jar_wydaj.text.t: "Talk." You draw on the map the way into the ravine, the path along the water and the spot where the lad with the stick falls asleep on watch. The Captain studies it without joy, then calls for the Sotnik. He pays you seventy groats from a chest that has no pay in it. "You did well. That's how it'll read in the report. Now go."

nodes.meldunek_wojna_beczki_cesarscy.tex.t: "The Imperials got the pitch? Wonderful, now they'll burn whatever takes their fancy." The Captain sighs. "Thank you. I didn't know one thanked a man for things like this."

nodes.meldunek_wojna_beczki_jarnowianie..t: "The Jarnowians got the barrels? Very well." The Captain quietly puts down his mug. "We'll remember that. Not you, us."

nodes.meldunek_wojna_beczki_rzeka.text.t: "Into the river?" The Captain snorts, then laughs for real, for the first time since you've known him. "Nobody gets any pitch. Both sides. I see now why they say you're dangerous."

nodes.meldunek_wojna_dezerterzy_puszczen.t: "The Lieutenant believed you? Rogala doesn't believe his own mother." The Captain shakes his head. "Fine. Let's leave it as it is."

nodes.meldunek_wojna_dezerterzy_tomasz.t.t: "Tomasz saved them? Tomasz?" The Captain slowly nods. "A good man. Just not made for war, and that makes him better than the rest of us."

nodes.meldunek_wojna_dezerterzy_wydani.t.t: "You handed them over? I knew you'd be good for this work." The Captain doesn't smile. "But I'll remember you can do it."

nodes.meldunek_wojna_dezerterzy_wykupien.t: "You bought them out? From your own pocket?" The Captain stares for a long moment. "You're mad. But in the right direction."

nodes.meldunek_wojna_most_otwarty.text.t: "You left it open?" The Captain glances at the map. "Well, the river is wide. And we've got our patrols. Fine, I know what to do."

nodes.meldunek_wojna_most_strzezony.text.t: "Spent the night on the bridge? Good. I'll send someone to stay there for good." The Captain puts down his pen. "Well done, wanderer."

nodes.meldunek_wojna_most_zerwany.text.t: The Captain is silent for a long while. "You tore down the Bridge on the Grey. The only bridge on the river." He wipes his eyes. "Well, at least now I know nobody's crossing it at night."

nodes.meldunek_wojna_ranni_lupy.text.t: The Captain looks at the sack, then at you. "Well, somebody has to do it." He looks away. "Don't tell the healer."

nodes.meldunek_wojna_ranni_swoi.text.t: "Only our own? I see, practical." The Captain shrugs. "War is a practical business. I'm not sure that's a compliment."

nodes.meldunek_wojna_ranni_wszyscy.text.t: "All of them? You took them all?" The Captain looks at you for a long time. "The healer told me. I didn't believe her. Good work."

nodes.meldunek_wojna_studnia_czysta.text.t: "You cleaned the well? Somebody's watering horses there now without asking permission." The Captain nods. "Good. That means they're not fighting."

nodes.meldunek_wojna_studnia_zasypana.te.t: "You filled it in?" The Captain raises his brows. "Well, fewer problems for the patrols. More for the people who live there. That's what comes of deciding for others."

nodes.meldunek_wojna_studnia_zatruta.tex.t: The Captain goes quiet. "You poisoned it?" He says nothing for a while, then pushes the map aside. "I'm not asking for details. Just tell me who's going to drink." You don't answer.

nodes.meldunek_wojna_zold_oddany.text.t: "All of it got there? You checked twice? Fine, first time I've met a man with nothing to hide." He jots it in the notebook and says nothing more.

nodes.meldunek_wojna_zold_podzielony.tex.t: "Took half, did you? You know that's against regulations?" The Captain stares at the roof of the tent. "Fine. The fewer who find out, the better."

nodes.meldunek_wojna_zold_zatrzymany.tex.t: The Captain looks at you like rain at haymaking. "Kept some? Well, at least that's honest. The garrison will know whom to thank." There's neither reproach nor surprise in his voice.

nodes.poznanie.text.t: "Report in? Wonderful, one more who reports in and doesn't know what for." The Captain looks you up and down. "Fine. The Crossing on the Grey, the burnt village, the battlefield, the Border Fort Ruins, two camps, ours and the Jarnowian one. All of it within a day's walk. The notice board has jobs I never got round to or didn't want to. Do three, and we'll talk about something serious."

nodes.stolica.options.[jade_zold].text.t: I'm going. I'm leaving the chest.

nodes.stolica.text.t: The Captain leans on the table. "Off, then? Mind you, what isn't reported might as well not have been done. Whatever you've got on paper with me, report it now, because nobody will hold you to account on the road. And if you're carrying anything of mine, it stays here."

nodes.sytuacja.text.t: "The war? The Emperor thinks he's winning because nobody's talked him out of it. The Jarnowians think they're winning because they've got powder. And we, in between, think we'll live to see spring. Somebody got it wrong, and now men are dying so nobody finds out who." The Captain rubs his eyes. "Orders come from Ulfgród that nobody reads to the end. If you've got the feeling someone's pulling strings, you're right. I just don't know whose."

nodes.sztab.options.[jar_list].text.t: The deserters in the ravine want to come back with a letter.

nodes.sztab.options.[jar_wydaj].text.t: I know the way into the ravine.

nodes.sztab.options.[poznanie].text.t: I came to report in. Where can I be of use?

nodes.sztab.options.[stolica].text.t: I'm ready to ride to the capital.

nodes.sztab.options.[sytuacja].text.t: What's the situation at the front?

nodes.sztab.options.[wywiad_falsz].text.t: The Jarnowians bought a bad road from me.

nodes.sztab.options.[wywiad_prawda].text.t: I hear there's bad news from the crossing?

nodes.sztab.options.[wzgorze].text.t: What's beyond the hills to the east?

nodes.sztab.text.t: The Captain stands over a map he hasn't read for an hour. A mug of cold tea on the table, a notebook full of crossed-out lines. "Keep it short. Or say nothing, damn it, I've got enough on my head."

nodes.wyjazd.text.t: The Captain seals the letter with wax and presses it into your hand. "To Ulfgród. Three days' ride if you don't get lost. Give it to someone who can read. Tell them the front is holding, but not for long. And that the men here aren't blind." He purses his lips. "Go. You've done what you could here."

nodes.wyjazd_skrzynia.text.t: The Captain seals the letter with wax and presses it into your hand. "To Ulfgród. Three days' ride if you don't get lost. Give it to someone who can read. Tell them the front is holding, but not for long. And that the men here aren't blind." He purses his lips. "Go. You've done what you could here."

nodes.wywiad_falsz.text.t: The Captain looks up from the map. "Forty Jarnowians at the fort on the Old Road. Command writes it off as their stupidity." He studies you, then takes sixty groats from the drawer. "I'm not asking how they knew which way to go. But the chest adds up, and I like it when it adds up."

nodes.wywiad_prawda.text.t: The Captain doesn't raise his eyes. "Three wagons of powder at the crossing. The drivers too. Somebody gave them the route and the hour." He crosses something out in the notebook so hard the paper tears. "I'm looking for who. When I find them, there'll be no talking. Anything else?"

nodes.wywiad_proch.text.t: The Captain stops rubbing his forehead. "Wet powder. Nine barrels." For the first time in a long while something twitches at his lips. "We heard a volley that coughed. Forty groats. I've got no more, and I simply don't believe you anyway."

nodes.wzgorze.text.t: "Gallows Hill? Three days' march. Old gallows, stone circles, and a keeper who remembers who hung on them. If you want peace, it's a good place. If you want work, also." The Captain shrugs. "They come back different. Some don't come back at all."
